back: RCOOR′: formed from a carboxylic acid RCOOH and an alcohol R′OH.
Alkyl group from the alcohol + -oate from the acid: CH₃COOC₂H₅ is ethyl ethanoate.
Acid + alcohol, a few drops of concentrated H₂SO₄ (catalyst), heat under reflux; reversible.
Dilute HCl or H₂SO₄, reflux: reversible → acid + alcohol.
NaOH(aq), reflux: complete → carboxylate salt + alcohol.
Alkaline hydrolysis of a fat or oil, giving soap (fatty-acid salts) and propane-1,2,3-triol.
Triesters of propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol) with long-chain fatty acids.
Solvents (ethyl ethanoate), flavourings (3-methylbutyl ethanoate: banana), perfumes.
Kc = [ester][water] ÷ ([acid][alcohol]); no units, volume cancels; about 4 for ethyl ethanoate.
